# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** Scottsford, New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Pettifer is a low-stature, heavy-set man who is completely bald except for a small strip of hair around his ears. When angry, his round face turns violet and his bulging light blue eyes protrude from his skull. He later appears neat, cleanly shaven, and with his remaining hair attentively cut.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046)_

## Personality

Mr. Pettifer is an eccentric, highly candid, and stubborn man who prides himself on speaking bluntly and truthfully to others. Although quick-tempered, impetuous, and stingy, he is deep down friendly, hospitable, and capable of holding deep affection for his companions. He appreciates neatness when enforced by his wife and takes a philosophical view on life and change.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P35](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0035), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)_

## History

After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation as an eccentric bachelor due to his irregular meals, unorthodox dishwashing methods, stinginess toward church and mission donations, and ownership of a cursing parrot named Nutmeg. In August, he burst into the Abernethy yard in a fury over their Jersey cow grazing in his oats, confronting Nell Harcourt. Soon after, Nell mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's Jersey cow to a buyer; when she came over to apologize and offer a frosted cake as a peace offering, he graciously agreed to trade cows and invited her to tea, beginning a close friendship. He occasionally conversed with Nell on his veranda, teased her about her teaching methods, and allowed young Robin to help him haul dulse. During a severe lightning storm, Nutmeg was killed when a strike hit the kitchen chimney and overturned the cage, leaving Mr. Pettifer grieving. Shortly after, a joke newspaper entry prompted his estranged wife, Emily, to arrive in Brierley, where they reconciled and resumed living together. Under Emily's domestic management, Mr. Pettifer began dressing neatly, regularly attending church, contributing to the minister's pay, and keeping his home clean.

## Background by volume

- Lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his housekeeping was managed by his sister until her death  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Married Emily Scott and took a two-week honeymoon in St. John  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Received his parrot Nutmeg from his brother, a seafaring man  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily over her obsessive housecleaning and dislike of Nutmeg, subsequently moving to Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Purchased the western neighboring property of the Abernethys in Brierley from Robert Bell  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> Tut, tut, miss, do not utter a single further word regarding it. It is immaterial . . . utterly immaterial. Misfortunes are bound to occur. On occasion, I am overly impetuous myself, miss . . . much too impetuous. However, I am unable to refrain from voicing my exact thoughts, and people are required to accept me as I am. Now, had that cow gotten into my cabbages . . . yet do not dwell on it, she did not, hence everything is fine. Because you wish to dispose of her, I believe I would prefer taking your cow in trade.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> I’m a crabbed, lonesome, crusty old chap, but I feel young again because of something about that little girl . . . and having that sensation repeated once in a while is something I’d like, since it’s so pleasant.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> That old bother Agatha Sowerby dropped by once more today, nagging me to contribute money for purchasing a vestry room carpet. My hatred for that woman exceeds my feelings for anyone else I am acquainted with. In merely six words, she is capable of compressing an entire sermon—complete with text, commentary, and application—and launching it at your head as if it were a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> Nutmeg won’t be calling you names again, Nell, poor thing  <sub>[v2 c24 P44](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0044)</sub>

> Modifications are not entirely agreeable, yet they are wonderful affairs. A couple of years is roughly sufficient time for circumstances to remain completely unchanged. Should they remain stationary for any greater duration, they could become covered in moss.  <sub>[v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)</sub>
